description:
memory.rs:484-532 — MemoryBackend::query_objects has _filter, _sort parameters. The function builds the full id list (sorted by id), applies position/limit pagination, and returns the slice. The filter is ignored. The sort is ignored.

Why this is borderline correctness rather than pure elegance: a user calling /query with a filter against the MemoryBackend will get the entire account's metadata back, paginated. The filter is silently ignored. The user thinks they're filtering by relatedType='Email'; they receive everything.

The current 'oops we ignored your filter' behavior is masked because tests/metadata_tests.rs has NO /query tests (see JMAP-ayoz.6). Anyone writing a Metadata/query test against this MemoryBackend will surface the bug immediately.

The behavior is wrong because:
1. MemoryBackend's stated purpose (per its rustdoc at memory.rs:7-13) is to be 'a documented, complete, source-readable implementation of the MetadataBackend trait to study when writing a real (database-backed) backend.' A contributor studying it for /query semantics gets a misleading template.
2. The PLAN.md explicitly lists Metadata/query test cases that this impl cannot satisfy.

Why P3 not P2: it's a known incomplete-impl rather than a regression. The rustdoc and PLAN.md both already disclaim production-readiness; the gap is between disclaimed-incomplete and actually-incomplete.

Fix options:
a) Implement the filter and sort honestly. relatedType, @type, isPrivate, relatedIds, textMatch (case-insensitive contains over vendor/extra fields) — all of these are simple in-memory operations against the cached Metadata. Sort on the five mandated keys.
b) Loudly fail: return BackendSetError-equivalent for query (but query doesn't use SetError) — at minimum log a warning, or panic in test builds.
c) Document the gap on MemoryBackend's rustdoc: 'query_objects ignores filter and sort; returns all account metadata.' This is the cheapest fix and matches the workspace's existing convention of disclaiming reference-impl limitations.

Recommend (a) — the impl is small (50-100 lines of straightforward predicate code) and unblocks JMAP-ayoz.6's test suite. The whole point of the MemoryBackend is to be the canonical study reference.

If (a) is out of scope for this review epic, file as a child of JMAP-06zp (the metadata-types/server umbrella) and require (c) in the meantime — current behavior is silently misleading.
title: MemoryBackend.query_objects ignores filter/sort entirely; returns full account sorted by id
